# GYMNASTICS

From ancient Greece to the modern Olympic stage, gymnastics has evolved into one of the most captivating sports in the world. Modern gymnastics took shape in the early 1800s, thanks to Friedrich Ludwig Jahn, known as the “Father of Modern Gymnastics.”

By the mid-1800s, gymnastics clubs began forming in Germany and the United States, paving the way for organized competition. These early movements ultimately led to gymnastics being featured in the first modern Olympic Games in 1896 — a defining moment that set the stage for more than a century of Olympic excellence.

## Gymnastics in the Olympics

![Image 9: Helen Maroulis is crying as she holds as American flag](blob:http://localhost/96936b895e7b34d3cc1948a285b17c18)

Gymnastics made its Olympic debut at the 1896 Athens Games for men and expanded to include women’s gymnastics at the Amsterdam 1928 Olympic Games.

Throughout the decades, the sport has given rise to unforgettable Olympic moments, from Nadia Comăneci’s perfect 10s to Kerri Strug’s one-legged vault and Simone Biles’ record-breaking 11-medal run.

### Types of Gymnastics in the Olympics

There are three main types of gymnastics featured in the Summer Olympic Games, each with its own style, rules, and audience appeal: **Artistic,****Rhythmic, and****Trampoline.**

#### Artistic Gymnastics

*   **Most popular type** of Olympic gymnastics.
*   **Feature both male and female** competitions.
*   **Men’s Events**: Floor Exercise, Pommel Horse, Still Rings, Vault, Parallel Bars, and Horizontal Bar.
*   **Women’s Events**: Vault, Uneven Bars, Balance Beam, and Floor Exercise.
*   **Competition Formats**: Team Competition, All-Around Competition, and Individual Competition.

#### Rhythmic Gymnastics

*   **Feature only female** competitions.
*   **Ribbons, hoops, and balls** are used by athletes.
*   **Events**: Rope, Hoop, Ball, Clubs, and Ribbon
*   **Competition Formats:**Individual All-Around and Group All-Around

#### Trampoline Gymnastics

*   **Features both male and female** competitions (this began at the Sydney 2000 Olympics).
*   **Competition Formats:**Individual Trampoline (The only type of trampoline gymnastics showcased at the Olympics.)

### Fun Facts on Olympic Gymnastics

*   The **top three countries with the most Olympic medals** in artistic gymnastics history for **women** are Soviet Union, Romania, and the United States. For **men**, they are Soviet Union, Japan, and the United States.
*   The **open-ended scoring****system for artistic gymnastics introduced in 2006****replaced the traditional “perfect 10” scoring format**, which added a limitless difficulty score to reward complex and innovative routines.
*   **Rhythmic gymnastics** was introduced at the **[Los Angeles 1984 Olympic Games](https://usopm.org/los-angeles-1984-olympic-games/)**and **trampoline gymnastics** was introduced at the [**Sydney 2000 Olympic Games.**](https://usopm.org/sydney-2000-olympic-games-american-gold-medalists/)

### Famous Olympic Gymnasts from Team USA

From historic champions to record-breaking icons, Team USA’s gymnasts have shaped the story of Olympic gymnastics and inspired generations — from perfect 10s to barrier-breaking firsts — defining Team USA gymnastics history on the world stage. Meet the Olympic legends whose talent and determination continue to raise the bar for athletes everywhere.

#### Top Female Olympic Gymnasts

##### Shannon Miller

![Image 10: Peter Vidmar - famous male gymnast from team USA](blob:http://localhost/bbcd34cc34386ed62cb5cc8ae42e5127)

[**Miller**](https://usopm.org/shannon-miller/) is one of the most decorated gymnasts in the United States, with seven Olympic medals. She competed in the Olympics as a member of the [**1996 U.S. women’s gymnastics team**](https://usopm.org/1996-womens-gymnastics-team/), known as the “Magnificent Seven,” that won the team gold medal. She was later inducted into the U.S. Olympic Hall of Fame in 2006 for individual achievements and in 2008 for her team achievements.

##### Simone Biles

![Image 11: Simone Biles is focused on her jump on the balance beam.](blob:http://localhost/a776d565a4fd37d7af7f8752503c942d)

Considered one of the greatest gymnasts of all time, Simone Biles is a 3-time Olympian and the most decorated gymnast in history with 11 Olympic medals. Her achievements span Rio 2016 (4 golds, 1 bronze), Tokyo 2020 (1 silver, 1 bronze), and at Paris 2024 Olympic Games, where she won gold in the team, individual all-around, and vault, and a silver in the floor exercise.

##### Mary Lou Retton

![Image 12: shannon miller famous scrunchy at USOPM](blob:http://localhost/74d408d24fb2e716fd42d8bf34cec131)

At the Los Angeles 1984 Olympic Games, [**Retton**](https://usopm.org/mary-lou-retton/) collected five Olympic medals— one gold, two silver, and two bronze — making her the most decorated American athlete of those Games. She also made history as the first American to win the individual all-around gold in gymnastics, thanks to scoring perfect 10s on the floor exercise and vault.

##### Dominique Dawes

![Image 13: Peter Vidmar - famous male gymnast from team USA](blob:http://localhost/bbcd34cc34386ed62cb5cc8ae42e5127)

Dominique Dawes is a three-time Olympian and a legend in U.S. gymnastics, earning four Olympic medals—including gold in the team event. She made history as a member of the iconic 1996 U.S. women’s gymnastics team, the “[**Magnificent Seven**](https://usopm.org/1996-womens-gymnastics-team/),” by being the first African-American gymnast to win an individual Olympic medal.

##### Gabby Douglas

![Image 14: Peter Vidmar - famous male gymnast from team USA](blob:http://localhost/bbcd34cc34386ed62cb5cc8ae42e5127)

[**Gabby Douglas**](https://usopm.org/gabby-douglas/) is a two-time Olympian and three-time Olympic gold medalist, best known as the first African-American gymnast to win the Olympic all-around gold medal at the London 2012 Olympic Games. She also became the first U.S. women’s all-around champion to qualify for a second Olympic team.

##### Kerri Strug

![Image 15: kerry strug - famous female gymnast in the olympics](blob:http://localhost/2f5e5e429b34035c80c3cb69ce4f8ba1)

Kerri Strug was a core member of the 1996 “Magnificent Seven,” the first U.S. women’s team to win Olympic gold. She famously secured the gold in the team final by performing her second vault on an injured ankle, a moment of raw courage that became one of the most iconic, unforgettable, and newsworthy feats of the Atlanta 1996 Olympic Games.

#### Top Male Olympic Gymnasts

##### Bart Connor

![Image 16: Peter Vidmar - famous male gymnast from team USA](blob:http://localhost/bbcd34cc34386ed62cb5cc8ae42e5127)

Bart Conner is a two-time Olympic gold medalist and one of the most accomplished male gymnasts in U.S. history. At the 1984 Los Angeles Olympic Games, he helped lead Team USA to its [**first men’s team gold in 80 years**](https://usopm.org/1984-mens-gymnastics-team/) and earned an individual gold on parallel bars.

##### Mitch Gaylord

![Image 17: Peter Vidmar - famous male gymnast from team USA](blob:http://localhost/bbcd34cc34386ed62cb5cc8ae42e5127)

Mitch Gaylord made history at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympic Games, where he won four medals — including gold in the team event, silver in vault, and bronze in rings and parallel bars. He was the first U.S. male gymnast to score a perfect 10 at the Olympics.

##### Peter Vidmar

![Image 18: Peter Vidmar - famous male gymnast from team USA](blob:http://localhost/bbcd34cc34386ed62cb5cc8ae42e5127)

A steady leader and technical genius, [**Peter Vidmar**](https://usopm.org/peter-vidmar/) captained the 1984 U.S. men’s gymnastics team to its historic team gold medal — the first ever for the country. He also captured individual gold on pommel horse and silver in the all-around.

##### Paul Hamm

Paul Hamm, one of the most decorated American gymnasts of his generation, made history once again as part of the 2024 U.S. Men’s Gymnastics Team at the 2024 Paris Olympic Games. His leadership and skill helped propel Team USA to earn its first team medal in 16 years

## Para Gymnastics in the Paralympics

While gymnastics is not an official sport in the Paralympic Games, para-gymnastics became an official discipline of the FIG at the 85th [**Fédération Internationale de Gymnastique**](https://www.gymnastics.sport/site/) (FIG) Congress. This is a crucial step towards the goal of seeing gymnastics included as a Paralympic sport at the 2032 Brisbane Paralympic Games.

## FAQ About Olympic Gymnastics

### What are the competition phases in Olympic gymnastics?

There are four phases of Olympic gymnastics competition:

1.   Qualification Round – Athletes compete to earn a spot in the finals (no medals yet).
2.   Team Finals – National teams face off for gold.
3.   All-Around Finals – The top gymnasts compete across all events to crown the ultimate all-around champion.
4.   Event Finals – Specialists go head-to-head on individual apparatuses for glory.

### How many teams qualify for the team finals?

The top eight highest-scoring teams qualify for team finals — for both men’s and women’s competitions — where they start fresh (scores reset) and compete for Olympic gold, silver, and bronze.

### How many gymnasts compete in all-around?

The top 24 individual gymnasts (12 women and 12 men) from the qualification round advance to compete in the all-around finals, with a maximum of two gymnasts per NOC.

# GYMNASTICS

From ancient Greece to the modern Olympic stage, gymnastics has evolved into one of the most captivating sports in the world. Modern gymnastics took shape in the early 1800s, thanks to Friedrich Ludwig Jahn, known as the “Father of Modern Gymnastics.”

By the mid-1800s, gymnastics clubs began forming in Germany and the United States, paving the way for organized competition. These early movements ultimately led to gymnastics being featured in the first modern Olympic Games in 1896 — a defining moment that set the stage for more than a century of Olympic excellence.

## Gymnastics in the Olympics

![Image 9: Helen Maroulis is crying as she holds as American flag](blob:http://localhost/96936b895e7b34d3cc1948a285b17c18)

Gymnastics made its Olympic debut at the 1896 Athens Games for men and expanded to include women’s gymnastics at the Amsterdam 1928 Olympic Games.

Throughout the decades, the sport has given rise to unforgettable Olympic moments, from Nadia Comăneci’s perfect 10s to Kerri Strug’s one-legged vault and Simone Biles’ record-breaking 11-medal run.

### Types of Gymnastics in the Olympics

There are three main types of gymnastics featured in the Summer Olympic Games, each with its own style, rules, and audience appeal: **Artistic,****Rhythmic, and****Trampoline.**

#### Artistic Gymnastics

*   **Most popular type** of Olympic gymnastics.
*   **Feature both male and female** competitions.
*   **Men’s Events**: Floor Exercise, Pommel Horse, Still Rings, Vault, Parallel Bars, and Horizontal Bar.
*   **Women’s Events**: Vault, Uneven Bars, Balance Beam, and Floor Exercise.
*   **Competition Formats**: Team Competition, All-Around Competition, and Individual Competition.

#### Rhythmic Gymnastics

*   **Feature only female** competitions.
*   **Ribbons, hoops, and balls** are used by athletes.
*   **Events**: Rope, Hoop, Ball, Clubs, and Ribbon
*   **Competition Formats:**Individual All-Around and Group All-Around

#### Trampoline Gymnastics

*   **Features both male and female** competitions (this began at the Sydney 2000 Olympics).
*   **Competition Formats:**Individual Trampoline (The only type of trampoline gymnastics showcased at the Olympics.)

### Fun Facts on Olympic Gymnastics

*   The **top three countries with the most Olympic medals** in artistic gymnastics history for **women** are Soviet Union, Romania, and the United States. For **men**, they are Soviet Union, Japan, and the United States.
*   The **open-ended scoring****system for artistic gymnastics introduced in 2006****replaced the traditional “perfect 10” scoring format**, which added a limitless difficulty score to reward complex and innovative routines.
*   **Rhythmic gymnastics** was introduced at the **[Los Angeles 1984 Olympic Games](https://usopm.org/los-angeles-1984-olympic-games/)**and **trampoline gymnastics** was introduced at the [**Sydney 2000 Olympic Games.**](https://usopm.org/sydney-2000-olympic-games-american-gold-medalists/)

### Famous Olympic Gymnasts from Team USA

From historic champions to record-breaking icons, Team USA’s gymnasts have shaped the story of Olympic gymnastics and inspired generations — from perfect 10s to barrier-breaking firsts — defining Team USA gymnastics history on the world stage. Meet the Olympic legends whose talent and determination continue to raise the bar for athletes everywhere.

#### Top Female Olympic Gymnasts

##### Shannon Miller

![Image 10: Peter Vidmar - famous male gymnast from team USA](blob:http://localhost/bbcd34cc34386ed62cb5cc8ae42e5127)

[**Miller**](https://usopm.org/shannon-miller/) is one of the most decorated gymnasts in the United States, with seven Olympic medals. She competed in the Olympics as a member of the [**1996 U.S. women’s gymnastics team**](https://usopm.org/1996-womens-gymnastics-team/), known as the “Magnificent Seven,” that won the team gold medal. She was later inducted into the U.S. Olympic Hall of Fame in 2006 for individual achievements and in 2008 for her team achievements.

##### Simone Biles

![Image 11: Simone Biles is focused on her jump on the balance beam.](blob:http://localhost/a776d565a4fd37d7af7f8752503c942d)

Considered one of the greatest gymnasts of all time, Simone Biles is a 3-time Olympian and the most decorated gymnast in history with 11 Olympic medals. Her achievements span Rio 2016 (4 golds, 1 bronze), Tokyo 2020 (1 silver, 1 bronze), and at Paris 2024 Olympic Games, where she won gold in the team, individual all-around, and vault, and a silver in the floor exercise.

##### Mary Lou Retton

![Image 12: shannon miller famous scrunchy at USOPM](blob:http://localhost/74d408d24fb2e716fd42d8bf34cec131)

At the Los Angeles 1984 Olympic Games, [**Retton**](https://usopm.org/mary-lou-retton/) collected five Olympic medals— one gold, two silver, and two bronze — making her the most decorated American athlete of those Games. She also made history as the first American to win the individual all-around gold in gymnastics, thanks to scoring perfect 10s on the floor exercise and vault.

##### Dominique Dawes

![Image 13: Peter Vidmar - famous male gymnast from team USA](blob:http://localhost/bbcd34cc34386ed62cb5cc8ae42e5127)

Dominique Dawes is a three-time Olympian and a legend in U.S. gymnastics, earning four Olympic medals—including gold in the team event. She made history as a member of the iconic 1996 U.S. women’s gymnastics team, the “[**Magnificent Seven**](https://usopm.org/1996-womens-gymnastics-team/),” by being the first African-American gymnast to win an individual Olympic medal.

##### Gabby Douglas

![Image 14: Peter Vidmar - famous male gymnast from team USA](blob:http://localhost/bbcd34cc34386ed62cb5cc8ae42e5127)

[**Gabby Douglas**](https://usopm.org/gabby-douglas/) is a two-time Olympian and three-time Olympic gold medalist, best known as the first African-American gymnast to win the Olympic all-around gold medal at the London 2012 Olympic Games. She also became the first U.S. women’s all-around champion to qualify for a second Olympic team.

##### Kerri Strug

![Image 15: kerry strug - famous female gymnast in the olympics](blob:http://localhost/2f5e5e429b34035c80c3cb69ce4f8ba1)

Kerri Strug was a core member of the 1996 “Magnificent Seven,” the first U.S. women’s team to win Olympic gold. She famously secured the gold in the team final by performing her second vault on an injured ankle, a moment of raw courage that became one of the most iconic, unforgettable, and newsworthy feats of the Atlanta 1996 Olympic Games.

#### Top Male Olympic Gymnasts

##### Bart Connor

![Image 16: Peter Vidmar - famous male gymnast from team USA](blob:http://localhost/bbcd34cc34386ed62cb5cc8ae42e5127)

Bart Conner is a two-time Olympic gold medalist and one of the most accomplished male gymnasts in U.S. history. At the 1984 Los Angeles Olympic Games, he helped lead Team USA to its [**first men’s team gold in 80 years**](https://usopm.org/1984-mens-gymnastics-team/) and earned an individual gold on parallel bars.

##### Mitch Gaylord

![Image 17: Peter Vidmar - famous male gymnast from team USA](blob:http://localhost/bbcd34cc34386ed62cb5cc8ae42e5127)

Mitch Gaylord made history at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympic Games, where he won four medals — including gold in the team event, silver in vault, and bronze in rings and parallel bars. He was the first U.S. male gymnast to score a perfect 10 at the Olympics.

##### Peter Vidmar

![Image 18: Peter Vidmar - famous male gymnast from team USA](blob:http://localhost/bbcd34cc34386ed62cb5cc8ae42e5127)

A steady leader and technical genius, [**Peter Vidmar**](https://usopm.org/peter-vidmar/) captained the 1984 U.S. men’s gymnastics team to its historic team gold medal — the first ever for the country. He also captured individual gold on pommel horse and silver in the all-around.

##### Paul Hamm

Paul Hamm, one of the most decorated American gymnasts of his generation, made history once again as part of the 2024 U.S. Men’s Gymnastics Team at the 2024 Paris Olympic Games. His leadership and skill helped propel Team USA to earn its first team medal in 16 years

## Para Gymnastics in the Paralympics

While gymnastics is not an official sport in the Paralympic Games, para-gymnastics became an official discipline of the FIG at the 85th [**Fédération Internationale de Gymnastique**](https://www.gymnastics.sport/site/) (FIG) Congress. This is a crucial step towards the goal of seeing gymnastics included as a Paralympic sport at the 2032 Brisbane Paralympic Games.

## FAQ About Olympic Gymnastics

### What are the competition phases in Olympic gymnastics?

There are four phases of Olympic gymnastics competition:

1.   Qualification Round – Athletes compete to earn a spot in the finals (no medals yet).
2.   Team Finals – National teams face off for gold.
3.   All-Around Finals – The top gymnasts compete across all events to crown the ultimate all-around champion.
4.   Event Finals – Specialists go head-to-head on individual apparatuses for glory.

### How many teams qualify for the team finals?

The top eight highest-scoring teams qualify for team finals — for both men’s and women’s competitions — where they start fresh (scores reset) and compete for Olympic gold, silver, and bronze.

### How many gymnasts compete in all-around?

The top 24 individual gymnasts (12 women and 12 men) from the qualification round advance to compete in the all-around finals, with a maximum of two gymnasts per NOC.
